newsitem.title: USA: Calif oil cos look to squeeze more from old fields.
newsitem.headline: Calif oil cos look to squeeze more from old fields.

text.p: Hoping to squeeze more oil from California's aging fields, state and oil company officials will meet here Thursday to share the latest advances in production technology.

Pacific Technology Transfer Council (PTTC), a newly-formed resource center for small oil field operaters, will sponsor a daylong conference on prolonging the lifespan of "marginal" wells, which make up 40 percent of the state's output.
"It's a mission to put the technology in touch with the operators,' said Iraj Ershaghi, director of PTTC and the University of Southern California's petroleum program.
Marginal wells -- which produce less than 10 barrels-per-day -- comprise about 170,000 bpd of the state's one million bpd output.
The wells produce a significant amount of revenue for the state and federal government, Ershaghi said, estimating sales at about $2.5 million a year.

As big oil companies leave California to invest in overseas fields, more of the state's production is pumped by small independents, such as Berry Petroleum Co, Benton Oil & Gas and even smaller companies.
"I wouldn't be surprised in 10 years, rather than having companies like Chevron, you'll be having "Mom and Pop" operaters running California," Ershaghi said.
The conference is entitled "Enhancing Oil production and reducing water cut.
